THE FINDING (HIGH) — a server-supplied ref name can inject into the git remote-helper protocol

Threat model: a malicious or compromised git server. This CLI ships a git remote helper (git-remote-entire) that speaks git's remote-helper protocol on stdout. Ref names come from the server's advertisement and are echoed into that protocol stream.

internal/remotehelper/githelper/list.go:60:

    line := strings.TrimRight(string(content), "\n")

Only TRAILING newlines are trimmed. The result is then emitted (around :112-119) as:

    fmt.Fprintf(stdout, "%s %s\n", value, name)

pkt-lines are length-delimited, so a hostile server can embed \n INSIDE a ref name. It survives TrimRight and goes straight into the protocol stream.

A PoC against a fake transport confirmed this. A ref named:

    refs/heads/ok\n<sha> refs/heads/injected\n\nok refs/heads/main\n

produced an injected blank line that TERMINATES THE REF LIST EARLY — truncating the real refs and the trailing "@<ref> HEAD" symref line — and left residue sitting in the stream exactly where canonical git reads the NEXT command's response. "ok <ref>" / "error <ref>" is precisely the shape of a push response, so a malicious server can plant a FORGED PUSH RESULT: git reports a push succeeded that did not.

FIX DIRECTION
Reject any advertised value or name containing \n, \r, or NUL. Fail the operation loudly rather than sanitising silently — a ref name with a newline in it is not something that legitimately occurs, and quietly stripping it hides a hostile server from the user.

Then check whether the same trust assumption exists at the other advertisement parse sites and fix consistently:
  internal/remotehelper/gitproto/gitproto.go
  internal/remotehelper/githelper/refadv_cache.go

RED TEST — write it first and confirm it fails
Feed a hostile ref name (one containing \n) through the parser / handleList and assert it is rejected rather than echoed into stdout. A test that demonstrates the truncation-plus-residue behaviour before the fix is the deliverable here.

OPTIONAL, only if the above is done and green
Unbounded reads of remote bodies in the same package — no cap on io.ReadAll(refs) (githelper/stateless.go ~:37), the receive-pack advertisement cache (refadv_cache.go ~:48), the ref advertisement (gitproto/gitproto.go ~:143), or per-ref lines growth (list.go ~:100). All on the clone/fetch/push path, so a hostile server can OOM the client. The project's SECURITY.md scopes out only LOCAL resource exhaustion, so a server-triggered OOM is in scope. The model to copy is gitrepo/alternates_rewrite.go: capped read, truncation explicitly tracked, callers forbidden from falling back to the uncapped original.

RULES
- LOCAL BRANCH ONLY. Do not push, do not open a PR, do not add a remote. Commit locally.
- Commit normally; entire is enabled and captures the session automatically. Never create checkpoints by hand.
- Before each commit: mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci
- Two traps in that sequence: (a) mise run fmt can rewrite Go into non-compiling code while lint still reports 0 issues — always run go build ./... after fmt; (b) mise run test:ci rewrites .opencode/package-lock.json — never git add -A, stage explicit paths.
- Never call git.PlainOpen / git.Open directly and never call go-git's worktree.Status() — see CLAUDE.md for why (reftable and alternates handling; a forbidigo lint rule enforces the second). Use the gitrepo package.
- When done, report: what you changed, the test that proves it, anything contradicting this brief, anything you deliberately left alone.
